newsitem.title: USA: Mass. voters have doubts about new Gov. - poll.
newsitem.headline: Mass. voters have doubts about new Gov. - poll.

text.p: The new Massachusetts governor, Paul Cellucci, dogged by allegations of personal financial problems, faces a strong challenge from unconvinced voters, according to a Boston Herald poll.
Only 14 percent of respondents were "very confident" of Cellucci's gubernatorial abilities. Twice as many, 28 percent, were "not very confident" of the new acting governor.
The poll of 214 registered voters, conducted Monday, has a margin of error of plus or minus 6.7 percent.
Cellucci will take the helm later today after Gov. William Weld steps down to fight full-time against conservative opposition to his nomination as ambassador to Mexico.
In the poll, a further 39 percent said they were "somewhat confident" in Cellucci, while the remaining 19 percent had no opinion.
The Boston Herald poll also showed weak support for one of his top rivals, Rep. Joseph Kennedy, who is expected to seek the Democratic nomination for the 1998 gubernatorial race.
Republican Cellucci leads Kennedy by 45 percent to 33 percent. Against Attorney General Scott Harshbarger, also running for the Democrat nomination, Cellucci trails 30 percent to 35 percent.
And among independent voters, Cellucci trounced Kennedy by 51 percent to 22 percent, but he split the key group evenly with Harshbarger.
"Kennedy has some trouble," Boston Herald pollster Kelly Myers said. "It's been a tough ride for Kennedy since last fall."
